title: Layer Three: Trial of Fate
next_chapter_hook: The instant the third page of the Tianji Record awakened, Chen Ji saw a brand-new branch of fate—and at the end of one of those branches stood someone he absolutely should not have seen.

text.content: In the puppet's hollow eye sockets, that strange light burned like phosphorescent flames in an abyss. It should have been a dead thing, yet it radiated a chilling gaze that pierced the heart. Chen Ji's steps didn't falter, his face still wore that harmless, foolish smile, but beneath the surface, a storm was raging. 'A person from long ago'—these words were like a fine needle, precisely piercing into the forbidden zone he least wanted to touch. The secret of the Tianji Record, the destiny of the inheritor—could these traces already have been left in this ruin? He lowered his eyes, concealing all sharpness beneath the skin of a废物. His tone was humble to the point of meekness: 'Senior is too kind. This young one is merely a menial servant. How dare I compare myself to any old acquaintances of the senior.' The words fell, but the puppet only let out an ambiguous low laugh, turned, and drifted deeper into the secret realm.

The entrance to Layer Three was hidden behind a collapsed altar. When Chen Ji stepped across that invisible boundary, the surrounding scenery abruptly twisted. He felt as if he had fallen into a river woven from silver threads, each strand extending toward a different future, intertwining and缠绕, yet converging at some point into a pitch-black core. That was—his death node. The Tianji Record quivered violently in his embrace, all three fragments of pages glowed faintly, and in their resonance, an aged voice rang in his mind: 'Layer Three, Trial of Fate. Gaze upon your heart, and you may pass.' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a rare gravity. 'Boy, I cannot help you through this one. The shackles of fate can only be severed by yourself.'

dialogue.content: 'The third page of the Tianji Record awakening at this moment is no coincidence.' Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed in his Mental Sea, carrying profound meaning. 'The shackles born of fate will ultimately be broken by the power of fate. But the price...' He paused. 'Are you prepared to bear it?'

text.content: Chen Ji offered no reply. His gaze was already firmly captured by a scene within the silver-thread river—a depiction of himself kneeling on scorched earth, a pitch-black longsword piercing his chest. Blood dripped down the blade, blooming into strange red lotuses on the scorched ground. His face held no pain, not even fear—only a deathly stillness. And behind him, a blurred figure stood. That figure's face was deliberately obscured by some force; only a pair of eyes burning with golden flames could be seen. Those eyes gazed directly at him, as if piercing through the barriers of time and fate. The inevitable backlash of fate—so that was what it meant.

The silver-thread river surged violently, countless scenes flickering past like a carousel before his eyes. He saw Su Qingyao bathed in blood倒在宗门大殿之上, saw his missing sister Chen Nian imprisoned in the depths of an abyss by chains, saw Ye Qing, the Demon Path Saintess, with blood tears flowing from those eyes that should have been bewitching. Each scene was a possibility, and every possibility led to the same terminus—his death, and the destruction of everyone he cared about. No! Chen Ji fiercely clenched his fist, his knuckles whitening from the force. Had he endured and concealed himself all his life, calculating for all beneath heaven, only to walk toward this predetermined ending? The Tianji Record burned in his embrace like a branding iron, the seal on the third page crumbling inch by inch.

'Interesting human...' That low voice rang out again, but no longer from the puppet—it came from all directions simultaneously, like destiny itself whispering. In the silver-thread river, a phantom slowly formed, taking the shape of an exact copy of himself. The figure wore the same coarse cloth garments, with identical features, aura, even that faint, lingering smile at the corner of the mouth. The only difference was those eyes—ink-black, fathomless, as if capable of devouring all light. 'You saw it.' The fate phantom spoke, its voice indistinguishable from his own. 'You felt it too. Fate has long been set. No matter how you struggle, the destination will not change.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stared at this existence that was一模一样 to himself, his lips slowly curving into a mocking arc. He gently patted the Tianji Record in his embrace, as if calming a restless cub, or perhaps confirming some source of confidence. 'Fate has long been set?' His voice was平静得近乎冷漠. 'Then let me ask—who wrote the script you call 'destiny'?'

text.content: The fate phantom hesitated slightly, then let out a low laugh. That laughter carried a hint of mockery, as if ridiculing an ant attempting to shake a great tree. 'You're clever, Chen Ji. Clever enough to see through the operating rules of this world.' The phantom strode forward, standing face to face with him. 'But clever people often die the earliest, because they always believe they can change something. The Tianji Record chose you—this is your honor, and your misfortune. Without exception, every inheritor throughout history has fallen on the path of 'changing fate'.'

Chen Ji did not retreat. He slowly drew out the Tianji Record from his embrace, the three page fragments slowly unfurling in his palm, emanating a soft yet mysterious glow. The seal on the third page was dissolving like melting snow and ice, revealing a brand-new rune structure—the ability of 'Causal Tracing,' capable of tracing the fundamental cause of any event, thereby finding that crucial node on the thread of fate. 'Every inheritor throughout history has fallen?' Chen Ji softly repeated these words, a sharp light flickering in his eyes. 'Then let me thank them, for paving this road for me.'

text.content: The third page of the Tianji Record suddenly blazed with dazzling golden light. Chen Ji felt an endless stream of information flooding into his mind, every chain of cause and effect laid bare before his eyes. He saw the origin of that 'death ending'—it was a trivial choice he had never cared about, a rainy night three years ago when he saved a dying youth in the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain. That youth was precisely the chess piece Li Zhao, placed by Ling Yuan at his side.

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes rolled, his originally straight spine suddenly hunching down. His whole person trembled, as if terrified out of his wits by the fate phantom's pressure. 'Senior, spare my life!' He thudded to his knees on the ground, his voice shaking incoherently. 'This lowly one is merely a menial servant, knows nothing, understands nothing!' The fate phantom predictably took the bait—a contemptuous glint flickering in those ink-black eyes as it stepped closer, one pace at a time.

text.content: Chen Ji abruptly stood up, his entire aura changing dramatically. That skin of a groveling废物 was shed like a snake's skin, discarded without hesitation. His eyes burned with an almost maddened flame as his hands formed an ancient, complex seal. The Tianji Record quivered violently, vast amounts of Heavenly Fate Value poured out like a breached flood, transforming into a brilliant pillar of light that shot toward the heavens. Under this pillar's impact, the silver-thread river shook violently, countless threads of fate snapping inch by inch.

The ability of Causal Tracing acted like an invisible scalpel, peeling away the outer garments of fate layer by layer. Chen Ji saw—the rainy night three years ago, the youth he saved was named Li Zhao, originally an Outer Disciple of the Tianqing Sect, but long since bought by Ling Yuan. Li Zhao's approach wasn't to harm him, but to plant a seed beside him. Over three years, that seed had silently grown under the nourishment of his 'waste aura,' eventually transforming one day into a blade piercing his heart. And the true target of that blade was never him—it was the Tianji Record itself. What Ling Yuan wanted wasn't his life, but the complete inheritance of the Tianji Record.

'So that's how it is...' Chen Ji let out a low laugh, that laughter carrying a sense of释然, but more a bone-chilling mockery. He finally understood why Ling Yuan had 'helped' him within this secret realm, why he had left that hint on the puppet. None of this was anything more than to lead him step by step into Layer Three, to awaken the third page of the Tianji Record—because only a complete, fully activated Tianji Record was what Ling Yuan truly wanted. What protection from the old sect master, what guidance from an old acquaintance—all bullshit! This old fox had been scheming against him from the very beginning.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji raised his head, staring directly into those ink-black eyes, the corner of his lips curving into a sharp arc. 'I underestimated you.' For the first time, the fate phantom's brow furrowed. 'No, you underestimated yourself.' Chen Ji walked forward slowly, each step crushing the silver threads beneath his feet, breaking those causal chains representing the 'death ending' one by one. 'Fate wants me dead?' His voice was平静得近乎诡异. 'Then I'll live. Not just survive, but live well. I'll see for myself how this 'destiny' you speak of gets torn apart by my own hands.'

text.content: The instant the third page of the Tianji Record fully awakened, Chen Ji felt a thunderclap explode in his mind. Countless pieces of information surged into his consciousness like a tide—the complete usage method of the Causal Tracing ability, the mysteries of fate he had never touched before. He saw every node on his thread of fate, saw the butterfly effect of every choice, and saw the key causal chain forming that 'death ending.' The origin was neither in the past nor the future, but—in the present. Every thought of his at this moment was determining the final direction of that fate thread. The fate phantom's expression finally changed; on that face identical to Chen Ji's, a emotion called 'wariness' appeared for the first time.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes. The Causal Tracing ability acted like an invisible thread, piercing through the barriers of time and space, reaching directly to that rainy night three years ago. He saw the youth huddled in the rain, saw his own outstretched hand—and then he saw himself withdraw that hand. Memories began to distort. That rainy night three years ago became an ordinary night. Chen Ji had never saved anyone; Li Zhao had never existed. All cause and effect, scattered like smoke.

choices.text: Return like for like—use the power of the fate phantom to backlash against itself
choices.description: With the power of the Tianji Record, forcibly graft the death ending's causal chain onto the fate phantom itself.

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, golden light blazing in both pupils, transforming into two substantial blades that pierced directly toward the fate phantom. His hands formed seals as he lowy intoned: 'Causal reversal, fate backlash!' The Tianji Record erupted with a stunning radiance, distorting that causal chain originally pointing to his death, and reversibly winding it around the fate phantom itself. The phantom let out a mournful wail; that face identical to Chen Ji's began to distort and collapse.

The moment causal reconstruction completed, Chen Ji felt a certain corner of his mind becoming empty. The memory of that rainy night three years ago didn't completely disappear, but became hazy and distant, like an old dream long forgotten. He knew this was the price of Causal Tracing—he had erased that fatal choice, but also forever lost certain things he should have remembered from that night. But it was all worth it. Because when the silver-thread river stabilized again, that originally pitch-black 'death branch' had completely vanished, replaced by a void full of unknowns. For the first time, fate had lost its direction at this node.

'You...' The fate phantom's voice shattered into pieces. That body woven from silver threads was rapidly disintegrating, dissolving into scattered starlight that vanished into the void. Its eyes were full of disbelief, as if questioning an impossible truth: 'How could you... break the编排 of fate...' 'Who told you I was merely 'breaking'?' Chen Ji stepped forward slowly, looking down at this dissolving phantom, the corner of his lips curving into a meaningful arc. 'I merely showed you another possibility. As for where this possibility ultimately leads—' He paused. 'You no longer have the right to know.'

dialogue.content: 'Well done, lad...' Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out once more, this time carrying genuine appreciation. 'I thought you would choose to clash head-on. Didn't expect you'd choose the smartest path—cutting from the cause, rather than entangling in the effect.' Chen Ji didn't respond, merely lowering his head to gaze at the Tianji Record in his palm. The third page had fully unfolded, displaying an ancient rune: 'Causal Tracing.' 'What's the price?' he asked. Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment before saying: 'You consumed thirty-five points of Heavenly Fate. But more importantly—you now see more than before.'

text.content: Before Mo Xiansheng's words even finished, Chen Ji understood their meaning. When he gazed upon the river of fate once more, the scene before him was already entirely different—he could not only see the direction of the future, but also faintly perceive the 'pushers' behind every thread of fate. In the distance of that blank fate, a blurred figure stood quietly watching him. That figure had no face, only a pair of eyes burning with golden flames—identical to what he had seen in the scorched earth phantom. The Heavenly Dao's Eye. It had always been watching. From the very beginning to the end, it had never looked away.

Chen Ji withdrew his gaze, a faint smile appearing on his face. That smile held no fear, no anger—only a leisurely composure bordering on playfulness. So what if the Heavenly Dao watches? So what if fate is weaving its web? Chen Ji never believed in any 'destiny' in this life. The third page of the Tianji Record awakened, Causal Tracing ability obtained, Ling Yuan's scheme laid bare, and顺便打破 that damned death prophecy—this trip into the secret realm had reaped huge rewards. He straightened his clothes, donned that skin of a废物 once more, and hummed a tune as he walked deeper into the secret realm. Destiny? Fuck destiny.
